Before the bridge, however, he sees a sign: the crossing is closed to bicycles today. A man with a yellow backpack points to a small path by the water. He says that Eren can reach a second bridge that way. The path is narrow and Eren has to push his bike for a while because many people are walking their dogs. On the other side he suddenly hears a whistle. The coach is by the water gathering balls. It turns out the playing field is not behind the first bridge but right here. Eren was almost in the right place. He helps the coach and goes to training with him.

Felix taps his phone, but the screen does not respond well to wet fingers. There are many people behind them. A helper asks them to come under a small roof. There Felix dries his hands with a tissue and finally finds the image. But the code is too small. Jan opens the confirmation on his own phone and shows both tickets. That way they get in before the first song. Later they sit on a wet bench and share an umbrella with a woman. To thank them, she gives them two pieces of cake from her bag.

But the picture does not show up because her grandmother is in the weather app. She only sees a large cloud. Ece asks her to tap the little house at the bottom of the screen. Now her grandmother can open the messages. She finds two photos, one of the balcony and one of a plant. Ece sent the second picture by mistake. He can get the kite down, but there is now a big hole in the paper. Yasmin still had a sheet of paper in her backpack. The boy has tape. They make a second, small kite together. It flies quite well even without a long tail. On the way home Yasmin gives the repaired first kite to the boy. She wants to return with the small kite at the next festival.

The man laughs: the dog is his and the door was shut by mistake. He lets it in. When the therapist arrives, the dog is already lying beside the chair.

When the water is back, one man still wants to sit outside. Nora leaves the table. They now use it every Tuesday when the weather is good. Esra always brings one pot then, but never two.
